children: KUALA LUMPUR, Malaysia--Shares of Mr. D.I.Y. Group (M) are lower in early trade Wednesday after it reported weaker third-quarter profits.
Shares of the Malaysian home improvement retailer fell as much as 5.3%. They were last down 4.3% at 1.00 ringgit, bringing their year-to-date loss to 35%.

Mr. D.I.Y. late Tuesday said its third quarter net profit was 6.4% lower, compared with the same period a year earlier, at 127.3 million ringgit, equivalent to $31.1 million, reflecting higher staff costs, depreciation of assets and continued investments in network expansion.
Revenue rose 4.8% on year to 1.26 billion ringgit, while its gross profit margin narrowed to 46.4% from 47.3% a year earlier.
Citi downgraded Mr. D.I.Y.'s rating to sell from buy and cut its stock target price to 0.81 ringgit from 2.10 ringgit, citing earnings headwinds.
Looking ahead, Mr. D.I.Y. Group (M) could see weaker gross margins and higher labor costs, Citi analyst Gan Huan Wen said in a note.
A weaker ringgit compared with the Chinese yuan is expected to push up inventory costs, as the retailer sources 65%-70% of its products from China, putting pressure on its profit margins, he said.
Gan also expects the minimum wage hike from mid-2027 to increase operating costs and reduce the company's annual net profit by about 4%.

CIMB also cut its stock target price for Mr. D.I.Y. to 1.35 ringgit from 1.89 ringgit and lowered its 2026-2028 earnings per share estimates by 9.6%-11.4% following the company's disappointing third-quarter results.
The lower valuation multiple reflects weaker earnings growth prospects amid intensifying retail competition, particularly from Chinese e-commerce platforms, analyst Walter Aw Lik Hsin said in a note.
However, CIMB maintained its buy rating on Mr. D.I.Y, citing its undemanding valuations.
